----Respondents
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Mohd. Akbar Tak
For Respondent No.1 : Mr. S.K. Bhati, P.P.
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Farjand Ali
Order 16/04/2024
1.

The instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing of FIR No.69/2023 dated 03.04.2023 of Police Station Kheroda, District Udaipur for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner prays for quashing the aforementioned FIR and all further proceedings in pursuant thereof.
3. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner for quashing of the FIR and all further proceedings in pursuant thereof.

4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the niceties of the matter, it is felt appropriate to direct that the petitioner shall not be arrested during the entire course of [2024:RJ-JD:16563] (2 of 2) [CRLMP-4201/2023] investigation.
Instead thereof, if offence is found proved, then the Investigating Officer shall inform the petitioner to appear before the trial Court on the date of filing of charge-sheet.
Udai Lal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:16563) on 16 April, 2024

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. On the day of filing of the charge-sheet and upon the appearance of the petitioner, he shall move a regular bail application under Section 437 of the Cr.P.C. and whereupon the learned trial Court shall release him on bail on the very same day; on the amount of surety and bond as it deems fit.
6.
Accordingly, the instant criminal misc. petition as well as the stay petition are disposed of.
7. Nothing precluded the petitioner to raise his grounds before the learned trial Court at appropriate stage.
